items.hint: Get the absolute value alone on one side before you split anything, and remember that the bars produce two separate equations.

items.stem: A student solves $|2x-1| \ge 7$ as follows. Case 1: $2x-1 \ge 7$, so $x \ge 4$. Case 2: $-(2x-1) \ge 7$, so $2x-1 \ge -7$, so $x \ge -3$. She reports the solution $[-3,\infty)$. Which correction is right?
items.hint: Look hard at the move from $-(2x-1) \ge 7$ to a statement about $2x-1$: what does dividing an inequality by a negative number do to the symbol?
worked: Case 2 divides by $-1$, which reverses the symbol: $2x-1 \le -7$.
A $\ge$ absolute value is an OR, so the solution is $(-\infty,-3] \cup [4,\infty)$.

options.text: The second case is unnecessary; the solution is $[4,\infty)$.
Case 2 must reverse the symbol to $2x-1 \le -7$, giving $x \le -3$, so the solution is $(-\infty,-3] \cup [4,\infty)$.
Case 2 should have been written $-2x-1 \ge 7$, giving $x \le -4$, so the solution is $(-\infty,-4] \cup [4,\infty)$.
Nothing is wrong; the solution is $[-3,\infty)$.

items.hint: An absolute value can never come out negative, so once you have candidate roots you must substitute each one back into the original equation.
worked: Check $x=-1$: the left side is $3$ but the right side is $-3$, so it is extraneous.
Check $x=1$: both sides equal $1$, so $x=1$ is the only solution.
